body:
N-31 BUILT (server, not walked), PR of branch task/N-31-retire-refs-of-deleted-lists (helper-n31, 15 Nov 2026). WHAT CHANGED FROM THE ITEM'S TEXT, AND WHY (each point is a test):
(1) A `playlist` row is NEVER purged, only its ENTRIES (90 days after the deletion). Reason, from the code: migrate_from_navidrome finds a source playlist by (owner, source_id) with NO deleted_at filter, so purging the row brings a deleted playlist back at the next "bring over my library"; import.playlist has a foreign key with no cascade; a create retried by a long-offline phone still gets the deleted row. The advisor agreed after seeing the evidence. So the phone still receives the whole `deleted: true` row, and nothing is synthesized for playlists in practice (the rule exists for both kinds: told deleted ONLY when NO row with that id exists at all, whoever owns it; the collaborative trap has three tests, shown red by mutation).
(2) A removed entry of a LIVE playlist is purged too (90 days), and the feed says {id, playlist, deleted: true}. The bare {id, deleted: true} of the design does NOTHING on today's phone: encore_writer.dart applyPlaylists has `if (e.id.isEmpty || e.playlist.isEmpty) continue;` before it deletes by entry id (proved by a Dart test on the real saved response). So migration 0016 adds change_log.parent (the playlist of an `entry` row), backfilled from the entries that exist, and library._touch REFUSES an entry row without it.
(3) An import's counts were computed from its entries: migration 0016 stores them on the import row (entries_purged_at, final_total/matched/unmatched/pending/kept) in the same transaction as the purge; finished (done, stopped, failed) and more than 60 days old by updated_at; a running import is never touched. The Encore app never calls GET imports/{id}/entries (it answers [] for an old import).
(4) migrate_from_navidrome now skips a source playlist the person deleted (without it, once its entries were purged, the playlist looked empty, add_entries raised not_found and the whole bring-over for that person failed: test red on the old code).
(5) change_log is NEVER pruned: that, not the 90 days, is what keeps an away phone correct. Written in library.changes, tombstone_purge.py, docs/18 and docs/17.
OPEN, FOR THE PHONE (not done, server only): after a tombstone drops the last entry of a song, the phone's row for that song is not dropped (dropUnused sees the ids a page carries, not those of entries a tombstone removed), and pull() reads the gone feed BEFORE the changes feed, so a phone that was away learns "gone" while its entries still hold the row. Fix on the phone: in applyPlaylists, collect the trackIds of the entries it deletes (by playlist tombstone or by entry id) and call dropUnused with them. Recorded in docs/34 CF-46 (Open, app). ALSO NOT SOLVED: an import whose `match` work failed stays `running` for ever and keeps its songs; an add_entries retried with a purged pe_ id after 90+ days offline would bring the entry back.
NOT CHECKED: nothing walked on VM 108 or a phone. To check on the bench: set deleted_at of a test playlist (and one removed entry, and an import's updated_at) to more than 90/60 days ago, restart, and watch "tombstone purge: removed N playlist entries and the songs of M imports" then "ref janitor: retired K song refs".
